predecessors.name: Tianwan
predecessors.text: most Tianwan territories (Chen Han page), Hubei, Hunan and Jiangxi

successors.name: Zhu Yuanzhang's Wu
successors.text: Zhu occupied and absorbed the Han territories in Hubei, Hunan, and Jiangxi by April 1365

ledger.x: Early 1360: Chen Youliang declares himself King of Han at Jiujiang.
June 1360: Chen murders Xu Shouhui and takes Tianwan's land.
June 1360: Chen Youliang proclaims himself emperor of the Great Han.
1361: Han and Wu fight over the Yangtze at Jiujiang and Anqing.
August 1361: the Han retake Jiujiang and Anqing.
September 1361: Zhu's fleet defeats the Han fleet and takes Jiujiang for good; it fails to take Hanyang.
September 1361: with Jiujiang lost, Chen Youliang holds out at Wuchang, his capital to 1364.
Early 1362: Nanchang surrenders and Zhu holds Jiangxi.
March 1364: the fighting ends at Wuchang.
March 1364: Chen Li surrenders Wuchang and the Han ends.

wars.name: Chen Youliang's war with Zhu Yuanzhang (Battle of Lake Poyang)
wars.outcome: Zhu wins: Jiujiang 1361, Jiangxi 1362, the Battle of Lake Poyang (30 August to 3 October 1363, Chen killed by an arrow), Wuchang surrenders March 1364 and the Han lands are absorbed by April 1365.

wars.name: Red Turban Rebellions
wars.outcome: Umbrella conflict; Zhu absorbs most rebel states and proclaims the Ming in 1368.

certainty.note: River and lake frontiers held by fleets; no page gives a boundary line.
